hints: At any moment, the next node of the answer is the smallest among the current front nodes of all lists. How can you get that minimum quickly every time?

A min-heap (PriorityQueue) holding the current head of each non-empty list, ordered by value. Repeatedly poll the smallest, append it, and push its successor. (Pairwise divide-and-conquer merging also gives O(N log k).)

1. Push every non-null list head into a min-heap keyed by val.
  2. Create dummy and tail.
  3. While the heap is not empty: poll the smallest node, append it to tail.
  4. If that node has a next, push it into the heap.
  5. Return dummy.next.

approaches.name: Collect and sort
approaches.idea: Copy all N values into an array, sort, build a list.

approaches.name: Merge one by one
approaches.idea: Merge list 1 with list 2, the result with list 3, and so on; early nodes get re-scanned many times.

approaches.name: Optimal: min-heap of heads
approaches.idea: Each of N nodes enters and leaves a heap of size at most k.

explain: For [[1,4,7],[2,5],[3,6,9]] the heap starts with 1, 2, 3. We poll 1 and push 4, poll 2 and push 5, poll 3 and push 6, and so on, producing 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,9. The heap never holds more than one node per list, so its size is at most k. Empty lists (or an empty array) are simply never pushed, giving null.
recognize: Merge k sorted sequences → keep the current front of each in a min-heap.
javascript: function mergeKLists(lists) { const a = []; for (let l of lists) for (let c = l; c; c = c.next) a.push(c); a.sort((x, y) => x.val - y.val); for (let i = 0; i < a.length; i++) a[i].next = a[i+1] || null; return a[0] || null; }
